newsitem.title: USA: Fed Vice Chair Rivlin says "tough call" on rates.
newsitem.headline: Fed Vice Chair Rivlin says "tough call" on rates.

text.p: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Alice Rivlin warned on Wednesday of the risk of higher U.S. inflation and said it was a "tough call" to decide whether the central bank needed to raise interest rates further.

"There seems to be little risk of the economy slowing down too much in the near term and sliding into recession," she said in prepared testimony to the House Banking committee just one day after Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan appeared before a House panel. "The risks seem higher on the other side -- that many of the factors holding down inflationary pressures will prove temporary," she said.
The Fed raised a key short-term interest rate in March for the first time in more than two years, bumping it up by a quarter percentage point. It has since held policy steady.

In deciding whether to raise rates again, Fed policymakers have to weigh the risk of slowing the economy unnecessarily against the risk of waiting too long and raising the threat of the economy overheating. "It's a tough call," Rivlin said.

On Tuesday, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan cheered financial markets by telling a House banking subcommittee that the central bank would raise interest rates if needed to head off inflation, but suggesting that might not happen anytime soon. Greenspan was testifying on Wednesday before the Senate Banking committee using the same prepared testimony as Tuesday.
However, Fed Governor Laurence Meyer, testifying with Rivlin at the House hearing, said the Fed must not wait until inflation takes off before acting to raise interest rates.
